minutes.headline: The meeting reviewed remote‑control product features, component choices, power options, and internal design.
summary: The team discussed defining the remote's functionality by the devices it controls, such as DVD players or TiVo, to broaden consumer appeal.
Research was cited indicating consumers are willing to pay more for speech‑recognition capability, positioning it as a high‑class feature.
A beeping feature was proposed to help users locate a lost remote, mirroring rival products.
It was noted that a smart chip is required for multifunctionality, or an additional chip would be needed for extra functions.
The smart chip was described as a programmed component that can perform a fair range of functions.
Cost concerns about an additional chip were dismissed, with the belief bulk purchasing from a newer supplier would keep production costs within budget.
Batteries were selected as the power source because they are readily available and standard for remotes, with the number depending on size.
Typical remotes use two AA or four AAA batteries, sometimes three, as a reference point for the design.
A large on/off button was recommended to accommodate an older target demographic.
The internal schematic includes a switch between the power source and the rest of the device, and an infrared bulb for communication with various devices.
Adding a second infrared bulb was suggested to indicate functionality without requiring users to stare at the primary bulb when the battery is low.

topics.title: Product functionality and speech recognition
points: Debated that functionality should be tied to specific devices like DVD players or TiVo to serve a wide range of consumers.
Cited consumer willingness to pay more for speech‑recognition as a premium feature.
Proposed a beeping locator feature similar to competitors.

topics.title: Design components and smart chip
points: Stated that a smart chip is needed for multifunctionality, otherwise an additional chip would be required.
Explained what a smart chip is—a programmed component capable of a fair range of functions.
Asserted that extra chip costs would not exceed budget due to bulk purchasing options.

topics.title: Power source and button layout
points: Selected batteries as the power source because they are easily available and typical for remotes.
Provided the standard battery configurations: two AA or four AAA, sometimes three.
Recommended a large on/off button to suit an older demographic.

topics.title: Schematic and infrared bulb function
points: Described the internal schematic with a switch and an infrared bulb for device communication.
Suggested adding a second infrared bulb to signal functionality without staring at the primary bulb.
